      "arc_periodic_stripe_tiling_from_sparse_stripe_clues": {

        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC periodic stripe tiling from sparse stripe clues",
        "content": "For ARC tasks where the input contains sparse full-width horizontal stripes or diagonal stripes and the output expands them into a full periodic tiling: identify each distinct nonzero stripe as a clue, determine its stripe-coordinate (horizontal rows: row index; down-right diagonal: k=column-row), and use the number of distinct clue stripes as the period. Each clue fixes the color at its coordinate modulo that period; repeat those colors cyclically across the whole grid, filling every cell (no zeros). For horizontal rows, output is constant across each row. For down-right diagonals, output is constant on c-r diagonals, i.e. output[r][c]=motif[(c-r) mod period]. Example from task-03e48a56: clues are color 5 on c-r=-5 and color 6 on c-r=-10, so two stripes imply period 2; even k gets 6 and odd k gets 5, producing a checkerboard. Examples showed row-stripe clue counts 4, 6, and 8 yielding periods 4, 6, and 8, and a five-diagonal motif yielding period 5. The motif may include duplicate adjacent colors; preserve clue phase from actual coordinates.\nAdditional confirmed instance for task-03e48a56: a 2x2 diagonal-clue grid [[9,3],[0,9]] outputs [[9,3],[3,9]]. The clue at c-r=0 is 9 and at c-r=1 is 3; repeating the period-2 diagonal pattern fills the zero at c-r=-1 with 3.",

        "content": "Continual-ARC task-03e48a56 solved with a modular tiling rule. Infer a period/orientation from sparse colored diagonal-line clues, then fill the entire grid using repeating color classes. For the 27x27 test, lines were slope down-right (constant c-r): color 5 on c-r=6, color 1 on c-r=16 and c-r=-7. Modulo 3, these clues cover all classes: 5 where (c-r)%3=0, 1 on residues 1 and 2. Output is fully filled (no zeros): cell(r,c)=5 iff (c-r)%3==0, else 1. Confirmed correct.\n\nRelated demonstrations establish the general pattern: (1) a 10x10 grid with horizontal uniform rows at indices 3..9 colored 6,3,5,3,8,6,5 and blank rows 0..2; output repeats this 7-row sequence cyclically, backfilling the top as 8,6,5. (2) a 20x20 grid with sparse anti-diagonal clues (constant r+c) colored 9 at sums 31 and 36, and 3 at sum 38; output is a full periodic tiling: 3 where (r+c)%3==2, else 9. (3) a 14x14 grid with uniform row clues 4 at row 0, 6 at row 10, 3 at row 11; output repeats period 3 by row index: 4 for r%3==0, 6 for ==1, 3 for ==2. General lesson: sparse placements can encode a periodic color field along row/column/diagonal coordinates; infer the orientation from the clue lines, find the smallest consistent modulus, assign colors from clue residues, and repeat over the whole grid.",

        "title": "Periodic ARC grid: extend colored line residue pattern",
        "content": "For this task family, a sparse set of colored straight lines encodes a periodic color pattern; complete zeros by repeating the pattern in the line-normal/phase coordinate. Infer the SMALLEST period p for which all clues at the same phase are consistent, then propagate the observed colors across the grid. For full-width horizontal bars, phase is row index mod p, and output repeats full-width rows vertically. Example: 25x25 bars at rows 4=3, 6=7, 17=9, 23=1: p=4 is the smallest collision-free period, mapping row residues 0=3, 1=9, 2=7, 3=1. For diagonal line clues slope +1, phase is (column-row) mod p; the output is the corresponding periodic diagonal-band tiling. Determine p by trying increasing positive periods and rejecting any that assign different observed colors to the same residue. Demonstrations: 13x13 horizontal stripes produced row period 7; 16x16 diagonal clues period 5; 26x26 diagonal clues period 8; 14x14 diagonal clues period 6. Preserve clue lines and fill missing residue classes consistently. Avoid guessing period from number of distinct colors alone: minimum compatible period worked for the solved horizontal case.",

In task-03e48a56, anti-diagonal stripe sums 2 and 28 were color7, sum33 color9; period=3 (number of distinct lines), so r+c mod3=0 ->9 and residues1,2 ->7.         "content": "For ARC inputs made of parallel uniform stripes, complete the periodic pattern using stripe-line coordinates. Identify and ignore the background (often 0). A stripe at coordinate k assigns its color to phase k mod P; fill every line of the same orientation at that phase with the assigned color. Preserve the stripe orientation. For horizontal rows, k is the row index. For diagonal stripes in the demonstrated cases, k=r+c. Example: horizontal stripes at rows 0:4, 7:6, 9:2, 14:7 give P=4 and phases [0:4,1:2,2:7,3:6], so output rows repeat 4,2,7,6. Another horizontal example has background 0 and foreground rows 0:5, 2:2, 3:1, 4:9, 5:9, 6:9, 8:9; P=7, phases give [5,9,2,1,9,9,9], repeated.       "arc_denoise_rectangular_color_patches_and_remove_stray_pixels": {
        "id": "arc_denoise_rectangular_color_patches_and_remove_stray_pixels",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC denoise rectangular color patches and remove stray pixels",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a uniform background and several filled rectangular patches contaminated by isolated pixels of other colors, preserve each underlying rectangle and its color, replace anomalous cells inside the rectangle with its fill color, and reset stray pixels outside all rectangles to the background. Determine rectangle bounds from the larger, coherent same-color block, allowing single-cell defects on a boundary; do not absorb clearly protruding single pixels if including them would require adding a mostly empty row/column.
